items.title: Fakhar Zaman eyes one last shot at World Cup glory
items.description: Fakhar Zaman knows exactly how it feels to win major trophies. He also knows how it feels to wait years for that feeling. The southpaw has seen it all; from hitting a century that etched itself into Pakistan cricket folklore and helped them win the 2017 ICC Champions Trophy — their last global title — as a 27-year-old, to heartbreaks in 2021 and 2022 and outright debacles at International Cricket Council events over the next four years. He will be 37 when Pakistan take their next shot at a major international trophy, the 2027 World Cup, set to be held across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. It will almost certainly be Fakhar’s last chance to help Pakistan end their ICC title drought. And it will be that not only for the Mardan-born batter, but also for his contemporaries, the likes of Babar Azam and Shaheen Shah Afridi. The generation basked in stardom after the 2017 triumph and runs to the 2021 and 2022 T20 World Cup semi-final and final, respectively. But a dip that began after 2022 has continued since. Success in bilateral engagements over the past year or so has pushed Pakistan up to sixth and fifth places in the Twenty20 International and ODI rankings, respectively, but the team is long overdue to show its mettle where it matters most. And Fakhar understands that. “We know it’s been quite a while since we’ve won a major tournament,” he told reporters on the sidelines of Pakistan’s training session at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Friday, ahead of their ODI tri-series opener against Sri Lanka. “We’ve reached finals and played in semi-finals, too. “But, obviously, the happiness you feel as a nation when you win a trophy is something you don’t get simply by reaching finals or semi-finals, no matter how many you play. “We’ve sat down and discussed this at length, and many of the players are taking it very seriously. God willing, we’ll give it our best, and we hope for Allah’s help as well. We’ll make every effort to bring this trophy back to Pakistan.” Pakistan’s road to the 2027 spectacle starts with the ODI tri-series, in which they will face a struggling Sri Lankan side and 2019 World Cup winners England in a double round-robin format. The first three matches of the series will be played in Rawalpindi, while Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium will host the remaining league games and the final, scheduled for October 31. Fakhar said Pakistan would go into the series with the 2027 World Cup at the back of their minds. The senior pro suggested the pitches had been prepared to provide conditions similar to those expected in South Africa, where the national side will play most of their matches. Pakistan’s squad for the tri-series also points towards a combination of four bowlers, six batters and one all-rounder — a balance generally considered suitable for South African conditions. “The combination for the 2027 World Cup is looking very good,” Fakhar noted. “You can see that in the way the wickets are being prepared as well. “Everyone has the World Cup in mind, and the team combination is looking excellent.” Fakhar believes Pakistan’s players joining the ODI camp after featuring in the ongoing President’s Trophy — the first-class domestic tournament featuring departmental teams — and the squad members’ overall international experience put them in good stead for the series. “The best thing is that all the players are coming off a first-class season,” said the 36-year-old. “They are in rhythm and have been playing long spells of cricket. “When you play first-class cricket, 50-over cricket doesn’t feel that long. But if you regularly play T20 cricket, the 50-over format can feel a little longer.” Despite Pakistan’s trophy woes over nearly a decade, Fakhar has continued to accumulate runs in the one-day format since his Champions Trophy heroics. In 92 ODIs, he boasts an average of more than 45 and has scored 3,861 runs. He will look to cross the 4,000-run mark, with Pakistan scheduled to play at least four matches in the tri-series. The side will also play a five-match ODI series in England in May next year ahead of the World Cup. “Speaking for myself, ODI cricket is my favourite format, so I’m particularly excited about it,” Fakhar said. It remains to be seen whether one of the most beloved players of his generation can close his career the way he began it. He will have the opportunity to do so in, as he put it, his favourite format.

items.title: Clôture du Forum international des SGG à Conakry : Le Réseau scelle l’ère de l’IA administrative
items.description: Les rideaux sont tombés ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026 sur le Forum international des Secrétaires généraux de Gouvernement, réuni dans un complexe hôtelier de la capitale. En présence de plus d’une dizaine de Secrétaires généraux venus de plusieurs pays d’Afrique et d'Europe, le ministre Secrétaire général du Gouvernement guinéen s’est réjoui de la présence de ses pairs durant ces trois jours d’échanges et de partage d’expériences. « Cette semaine, nous avons franchi un pas de plus. Nous nous sommes demandé comment rendre [nos engagements de la première édition] plus performants et quelle place l'intelligence artificielle doit y occuper. Nous venons d'Afrique et d'Europe. Nos pays parlent des langues différentes, héritent de traditions juridiques distinctes et vivent des réalités diverses. Pourtant, en écoutant les experts qui sont intervenus lors des huit ateliers – et que je salue au passage-, nous avons réalisé que nous exerçons le même métier : préparer le Conseil des ministres, veiller à la qualité des textes normatifs, conserver la mémoire des décisions et suivre leur exécution », a déclaré Tamba Benoît Kamano. Poursuivant son intervention, le ministre a rappelé le rôle névralgique des Secrétariats généraux dans la coordination de l’action publique : « Nous appuyons nos Chefs d'État et nos Premiers ministres dans l'impulsion, la coordination et le contrôle de l'action gouvernementale. Dans chacun de nos pays, nous sommes les gardiens de la continuité de l'État . » Il a ensuite mis en lumière les atouts pragmatiques de l’intelligence artificielle : « L'IA peut nous aider à retrouver en quelques secondes un texte enfoui dans des années d'archives, à repérer une éventuelle contradiction avant qu'un projet de décret n'arrive en Conseil, et à savoir à tout moment où nous en sommes dans l'exécution d'une décision. » Screenshot Avant de conclure, M. Kamano a tenu à remercier le président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, ainsi que le Premier ministre, pour leur accompagnement constant envers son département. Des recommandations ambitieuses et structurantes Prenant la parole à son tour, la Secrétaire générale adjointe du Gouvernement guinéen, Mme Seregbé Keïta, a donné lecture des recommandations issues de ces trois jours d’intenses travaux. Parmi les axes prioritaires figurent l'institutionnalisation du réseau international des Secrétaires généraux et la définition d'orientations communes pour un usage responsable, sécurisé et efficace de l'IA au sein de l'appareil d'État. Mme Keïta a résumé les travaux autour de quatre enseignements majeurs : L'IA comme levier de performance : Elle offre l'opportunité d'optimiser la continuité de l'État, d'accélérer l'instruction des dossiers et de renforcer la qualité des décisions publiques. Un encadrement éthique et juridique impératif : Son déploiement exige un cadre strict garantissant la protection des données, la traçabilité, la transparence et le maintien de la responsabilité humaine. La primauté de la qualité du droit : La performance administrative repose d'abord sur la modernisation des procédures normatives, l'accessibilité de l'information publique et l'évaluation des résultats. La force de la coopération inter-États : Le réseau des SGG constitue un outil précieux de mutualisation des expertises et de partage de bonnes pratiques adaptées aux réalités locales. La Déclaration de Conakry : éthique et souveraineté À cette occasion, les pays participants ont adopté une déclaration commune. Représentant le Tchad, Bourkou Dédé Elhadj a, au nom de ses pairs, souligné que ce texte marque une étape clé dans la pérennisation du réseau initié en avril 2025. Tout en s'inscrivant dans la lignée des orientations de l'Union africaine et de l'ONU, cette déclaration affirme l'IA comme une priorité d'action, sous la forme d'un engagement d'intention sans contrainte juridique ou financière directe pour les signataires. Selon le représentant tchadien, la Déclaration de Conakry pose des garde-fous éthiques clairs : Le contrôle humain obligatoire : L'IA reste une aide à la décision et ne saurait se substituer à la responsabilité ni à la signature d'un agent public. La souveraineté numérique : Les outils déployés doivent respecter le droit international et héberger les données gouvernementales sous contrôle national strictement sécurisé. L'inclusion et l'équité : L'intégration des langues africaines, l'accessibilité numérique et l'évaluation préalable des biais (notamment envers les femmes et les groupes vulnérables) demeurent des conditions indispensables pour une transformation digitale juste. Faut-il préciser que le thème de cette rencontre de trois jours à Conakry était : « L’Intellignece artificielle au service de la performance gouvernementale. »

items.title: Palestinians and US journalist injured by Israeli settlers in West Bank harvest attack
items.description: Dozens of masked settlers have attacked Palestinians and set fire to cars and olive trees during the annual olive harvest in the occupied West Bank. A BBC team witnessed one of several attacks in farmland near the Palestinian village of Abu Falah. A local official said the attacks had injured 12 Palestinians, including four dual Palestinian American citizens. A foreign journalist was also among those hurt. Driving into the area early in the morning, we came across the first signs of the violence: a stream of cars carrying wounded Palestinian olive farmers racing out along the narrow stony track, piled high with olive picking equipment, as smoke rose from several fires nearby. The bloodied face of Majdi Fheed peered out from the backseat of one car. “We were getting our olive trees and almost 15 Jewish guys … started attacking us with guns, with rocks, with special weapons. They hit me on my head [and] my neck – look, I am bleeding!” Yaser AlKam, a council member from the neighbouring village of Turmus Aya told me Majdi – an American citizen – was attacked by settlers with nail-studded sticks, and needed treatment for deep wounds on his head. His elderly mother was also injured. Another man ferrying the injured to hospital told us that settlers had attacked them with sticks while they harvested their olives, and had burned three cars – including one of his own. “As soon as we got to the land and put our things on the ground, they started to come, so we ran away” said a woman next to him. Asked about the violence, a US State Department spokesperson said they were aware of the reports. “We condemn criminal violence by any party in the West Bank and call for investigations, arrests, and convictions, of those responsible,” the spokesperson said. Watching the vehicles stream past her, 73-year-old Imm Khaldoun told me emphatically that, no matter what happened, she would always return to her land. “This is my land. It’s my right [to be here]” she told me. The UN says the past two weeks have already seen more attacks by violent Israeli settlers than during the entire harvest season last year. Olive picking in the West Bank is now a test of speed, with trees rapidly stripped of fruit as soon as the sun rises, before violent Israeli settlers attack. In another olive orchard nearby, we watched as dozens of farmers used power-tools to strip the trees as fast as they could – one eye on the ridge above us, where a group of settlers at a new illegal outpost had already gathered, and were watching the olive harvest below. Standing on ladders, the Palestinian farmers worked quickly, sending streams of olives onto the plastic sheets laid out under the trees. Three villages had come together to harvest these olives, the landowner Amin Khalil, told me, as a form of protection against attack. He said his land was now surrounded by seven Jewish settlements and outposts. All Israeli settlements are illegal under international law. Outposts – small encampments on hilltops – are illegal under Israeli law as well, but many still receive state support. “This is a hotspot – there are seven settlements around here,” Amin Khalil told me. “This year, all the people came together because when there are just a few people working alone at the edge of the village, the settlers attack. So all the families are working together today.” But the tactic doesn’t work today. As we watch, dozens of settlers, all dressed in black, begin moving down the hill towards us, setting fire to several groups of olive trees. There are shouts of panic from the Palestinian farmers, yelling for children to get out of the field. Some begin swiftly wrapping up the olives to leave. But with large numbers of people on both sides, the confrontation stalls into an uneasy stalemate. We see settlers with slingshots hurl stones towards us, and young Palestinian men running to throw stones in return. As Israeli forces arrive, the standoff explodes into action. Settlers begin running down towards us as the farmers swiftly retreat. Some Palestinians set off fireworks to try and push the settlers back. American journalist Heidi Levine of the Washington Post was injured in the attack. She described how dozens of settlers ambushed her as she was reporting at the scene. “I got jumped,” she said. “I was on the ground and they were kicking me and I was trying to hold onto my camera and my bag. I had my helmet and flak jacket on which protected me. They made me stand up and they kicked me again, and this went on for at least 10 minutes.” In a statement, Washington Post executive editor Matt Murray said Levine had been clearly identifiable as a journalist. “We are outraged by this unwarranted attack on a journalist doing her job and urge a thorough investigation and follow-through from authorities,” he said. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said personnel had been despatched to the area “following a report of a violent confrontation”. It said a female journalist had been injured during the confrontation. And that “all circumstances” surrounding the incident would be examined. As the farmers retreated, the sound of live ammunition cracked across the fields. It was unclear if settlers or Israeli forces were firing. Minutes later, Israeli forces began firing tear gas into the Palestinian fields to end the confrontation – a well-worn Israeli pattern of managing these conflicts. The UN says settler attacks on the olive harvest this year have so far killed one Palestinian and injured more than 120 others across the West Bank. Illegal Jewish outposts have mushroomed here over the past few years, clustering in closer around Palestinian olive groves. What we witnessed was part of a pattern being repeated day after day, as settler outposts here increase. The yearly olive harvest has become a litmus test of how the policies of Israel’s fiercely pro-settlement government are affecting Palestinians here, by presiding over growing violence by extremist settlers, and fuelling Jewish claims to the land.

items.title: Burkina: 320 millions de F CFA à partager à 79 structures de presse privée
items.description: Le Fonds d’appui au sport et à la presse privée (FASP) «Wassa Bondo» a procédé, ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, à la remise symbolique des chèques aux bénéficiaires de la subvention de l’État à la presse privée. Sur les 94 dossiers enregistrés pour l’exercice 2026, 79 structures ont été retenues pour se partager une enveloppe globale de 320 millions de F CFA. Un soutien financier pour consolider les médias privés et renforcer leur capacité à informer les populations. C’est l’enjeu de la subvention de l’État à la presse privée, dont les bénéficiaires de l’exercice 2026 ont reçu symboliquement leurs chèques, ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026 à Ouagadougou, lors d’une cérémonie présidée par le ministre chargé de la Communication, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo. Le ministre chargé de la communication, Pengdwendé Gilbert Ouédraogo À cette occasion, le ministre a réaffirmé la place incontournable de la presse dans le fonctionnement de l’État, particulièrement dans le contexte actuel du Burkina Faso. Il a exhorté les professionnels des médias à faire preuve de professionnalisme et d’engagement afin d’accompagner les efforts des autorités dans la poursuite de leurs objectifs nationaux. «La presse occupe une place incontournable dans le fonctionnement de l’État et dans la vie de la Nation. Dans le contexte particulier que traverse notre pays, nous avons plus que jamais besoin de médias professionnels, responsables et engagés, capables de contribuer à l’information juste des citoyens, à la sensibilisation des populations et à l’accompagnement des efforts de construction nationale. Nous encourageons donc les femmes et les hommes de médias à demeurer attachés aux exigences de leur métier et à la qualité de leur travail. L’État, conscient de cette mission essentielle, entend poursuivre ses efforts pour soutenir la presse privée et lui permettre de mieux remplir son rôle au service de la Nation», a-t-il déclaré. 79 bénéficiaires sur 94 dossiers examinés Cérémonie de remise symbolique de chèques aux médias bénéficiaires Pour l’exercice 2026, 94 dossiers ont été enregistrés entre le 1er et le 31 juillet, dont 92 provenant d’entreprises de presse privée et deux d’organisations professionnelles des médias (OPM). Les candidatures concernaient 10 télévisions, 53 radios, 22 médias en ligne, sept organes de presse écrite et deux organisations professionnelles. À l’issue de l’examen, 79 structures ont été retenues, soit 77 entreprises de presse et les deux organisations professionnelles. Remise symbolique de chèques En revanche, 15 dossiers ont été rejetés, principalement en raison d’insuffisances relatives aux pièces administratives et fiscales, aux autorisations d’exploitation ou à la régularité de la diffusion. L’enveloppe globale de 320 millions de F CFA est répartie entre les différentes catégories de bénéficiaires. Ainsi, 304 millions de F CFA sont destinés aux entreprises de presse privée retenues, contre 12,8 millions pour les deux organisations professionnelles. Le solde de 3,2 millions de F CFA est affecté au fonctionnement du secrétariat technique. Cette répartition vise à soutenir les différentes composantes du paysage médiatique privé, conformément aux critères réglementaires en vigueur. «Faire de chaque franc investi un levier de performance» La directrice générale de Wassa Bondo, Mme Ida Ouédraogo Pour la directrice générale du FASP «Wassa Bondo», Ida Ouédraogo, l’octroi de cette subvention s’accompagne d’une exigence de responsabilité dans la gestion des ressources publiques. L’objectif est que les fonds reçus produisent des effets concrets sur le fonctionnement des médias, leurs équipements et la qualité de leurs productions. «Cette subvention constitue une opportunité importante pour renforcer les capacités de vos entreprises et améliorer la qualité des services médiatiques offerts aux populations. Nous invitons donc chaque bénéficiaire à en faire une utilisation optimale, rigoureuse et conforme aux objectifs pour lesquels cet appui est accordé. Les ressources mises à votre disposition doivent contribuer concrètement à l’amélioration des équipements, au renforcement des capacités des équipes, à la production de contenus professionnels et à la modernisation de vos organes de presse. La pérennité de cet accompagnement dépend aussi de notre capacité collective à faire de chaque franc investi un levier de performance, de professionnalisation et de viabilité économique pour la presse privée», a-t-elle souligné. Au-delà de l’aide financière, le suivi des structures bénéficiaires et le respect de leurs obligations réglementaires constituent des leviers essentiels pour renforcer la transparence et garantir une utilisation efficace des ressources allouées. Les bénéficiaires face à l’exigence des résultats Le représentant des médias bénéficiaires, Adama Sougouri Au nom des bénéficiaires, Adama Sougouri a salué l’accompagnement de l’État, tout en mettant en évidence les défis auxquels les entreprises de presse privée sont confrontées, notamment les charges de fonctionnement, les besoins en équipements et les exigences liées à la transformation numérique. «Nous accueillons cette subvention avec reconnaissance, mais aussi avec le sens des responsabilités qu’elle nous impose. Pour les entreprises de presse privée, cet appui représente une bouffée d’oxygène dans un environnement marqué par des charges de fonctionnement importantes, des besoins croissants en équipements et les exigences d’une transformation numérique devenue incontournable. Il nous appartient désormais de faire preuve de responsabilité dans l’utilisation des ressources reçues, afin qu’elles se traduisent par des améliorations réelles dans nos rédactions, une production de qualité et une information toujours plus professionnelle au bénéfice des citoyens. Nous souhaitons que cet accompagnement se poursuive et contribue durablement à la consolidation d’une presse privée viable, crédible et capable d’assumer pleinement sa mission d’information», a-t-il indiqué. Professionnalisation et modernisation en ligne de mire Des participants à la cérémonie Au-delà de la répartition des fonds, l’exercice 2026 souligne la nécessité de mieux informer et accompagner les promoteurs de médias sur les conditions d’éligibilité et leurs obligations réglementaires. La transparence, l’équité et la rigueur dans le traitement des candidatures demeurent également essentielles pour conforter la confiance dans le mécanisme d’attribution de cette aide publique. À terme, l’ambition est d’inscrire la subvention dans une dynamique plus large de professionnalisation, de modernisation numérique et de consolidation de la viabilité économique des entreprises de presse privée. À travers le FASP «Wassa Bondo», l’État entend ainsi contribuer à l’émergence de médias mieux outillés et plus résilients. Pour les 79 structures retenues, le défi est désormais de convertir cet appui financier en progrès tangibles, tant dans leurs conditions de travail que dans la qualité de l’information proposée aux populations. Car, au-delà des chèques remis, c’est aussi la capacité de la presse privée à remplir durablement sa mission qui est en jeu. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Burkina: 320 millions de F CFA à partager à 79 structures de presse privée est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Audience du Président du Faso : Le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ confie une mission aux Étoiles du Faso
items.description: Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a échangé, ce vendredi dans la matinée du vendredi 16 octobre 2026, avec les Étoiles du Faso, des Ambassadeurs du civisme et les lauréats du Grand prix d’engagement citoyen. Le Chef de l’État a félicité ces illustres élus avant de les envoyer en mission où ils sont condamnés à réussir : « promouvoir le civisme, le patriotisme et que leur brillance se déteigne sur les autres Burkinabè ». Le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ a appelé les Étoiles du Faso, les Ambassadeurs du civisme et les lauréats du Grand prix d’engagement citoyen à sensibiliser leurs frères burkinabè afin d’impulser le développement du Burkina Faso Les hôtes du Président du Faso à cette audience sont de trois catégories : les Étoiles du Faso, des personnalités modèles dans leurs domaines d’activités, les Ambassadeurs du civisme qui sont des élèves lauréats du concours sur le civisme, et les lauréats du Grand prix d’engagement citoyen décerné à des personnalités modèles qui ont fait flotter le pavillon national. Conduits par le Ministre de la Justice, Camarade Edasso Rodrigue BAYALA, ces femmes et hommes de différentes générations se voient confiées une mission par le Président du Faso, Chef de l’État, le Camarade Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ. « Vous êtes condamnés à être des étoiles pour toujours, pour illuminer le cerveau des plus jeunes et de tous vos frères. Donc, c'est une mission qui vous est confiée désormais de pouvoir illuminer tout un chacun », a-t-il dit aux Étoiles avant de s’adresser aux Ambassadeurs : « Vous avez aussi une grosse mission. Et vous aussi, vous n'avez pas le droit à l'erreur de votre jeune âge ». Le Président du Faso, a également expliqué à ces « élus », la quintessence du civisme et du patriotisme, qui sont des valeurs fondamentales et un socle du développement. Pour le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, le patriotisme, c’est « l'amour que nous avons pour notre chère Patrie, l'amour que nous avons pour la terre que nos ancêtres se sont battus pour nous léguer, l'amour que nous avons à entretenir cette terre pour la remettre dans de meilleures conditions à nos enfants, aux générations à venir. L'amour que nous avons entre nous, citoyens du même pays, entre nos frères et sœurs. Nous devons aimer tout Burkinabè comme notre sang ». Cette audience se tenant dans le cadre des Journées nationales d’engagement patriotique et de participation citoyenne dont le thème porte sur la promotion du consommer local, le Chef de l’État, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ, a expliqué à ses hôtes, les enjeux. Le Ministre de la Justice, le Camarade Edasso Rodrigue BAYALA a annoncé que des conférences seront organisées afin de permettre aux personnalités de partager leurs expériences Le Porte-parole des personnalités, le Camarade Inoussa SARÉ a remercié le Président du Faso pour l’honneur et pris l’engagement, au nom de l’ensemble, à réaliser la mission qui leur est confiée « L’enfant intelligent achète les galettes de sa maman. Encore faut-il que la maman puisse produire ses galettes et que l'enfant intelligent les paie ? Mais ça veut dire beaucoup de choses. Pour faire des galettes, il faut qu'on produise. Voilà pourquoi partout où nous sommes, il faut qu'on arrive à produire ce dont on a besoin. Nous ne pouvons pas dire qu'on est patriote et continuer d'importer ce que nous pouvons produire nous-mêmes ici », a fait comprendre le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ. Le Porte-parole des Étoiles, le Camarade Inoussa SARÉ a remercié le Président du Faso pour l’honneur et a traduit l’engagement de tous les lauréats aux côtés du Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORÉ pour relever les défis. Direction de la communication de la Présidence du Faso

items.title: 'I am a normal human being': Khawaja Asif brushes off online trolling over AI-generated Marilyn Monroe riddle
items.description: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif on Friday brushed off online trolls who mocked him for responding to an AI-generated riddle featuring Hollywood icon Marilyn Monroe on the social media platform X. On Tuesday, the defence minister and PML-N stalwart replied to an AI-generated image of Monroe on X, which asked users to spot the one item that did not belong in the AI-generated image from the 50s. Asif reshared the post and pointed out that Monroe was wearing a smartwatch in the image. The original post shared by the defence minister has since been deleted. Subsequently, netizens questioned the propriety of the post, while Indian media also published articles on Asif’s online activities . On Friday, Asif was asked about the post and whether he operated his X account himself during an appearance on Geo News programme ‘ Naya Pakistan ’. “Two hundred per cent I operate it myself,” he said. “I have a personal life and a normal life. I am a normal human being; there is nothing special about me,” he emphasised, adding that he had “no pretences”. “They presented a riddle asking about what was amiss with this photo, something that should not have been present in 1956. And that was the smartwatch, so I wrote ‘watch’. What is non-serious about this?” Asif stressed that though he was the defence minister, he operated his own account “for fun” and asked: “Am I not Khawaja Asif? If I am the defence minister, should I abandon my identity — whether it be good or bad?”

items.title: [Vidéo] Félir, l’île où le quotidien patauge
items.description: À Félir (département de Foundiougne), l’eau n’est pas seulement une affaire de paysage. Elle envahit les maisons, complique les déplacements et rappelle, chaque année, la fragilité des conditions de vie des insulaires. Derrière la beauté du décor, les habitants attendent toujours des réponses concrètes à leurs difficultés. Car si Félir signifie « là où il fait bon vivre » en sérère, encore faudrait-il que les conditions soient réunies pour que cette promesse prenne tout son sens. Pour rejoindre l’île de Félir, il faut d’abord laisser Foundiougne derrière soi. À bord de la pirogue, le paysage change progressivement. En cette matinée, le pont Nelson Mandela, qui surplombe le département, s’éloigne au fur et à mesure de notre périple. Les dernières habitations s’éloignent, les bruits de la rive s’estompent et la mer prend toute la place. L’eau s’étend à perte de vue, seulement interrompue par quelques embarcations qui avancent lentement. Le moteur de la pirogue ronronne tandis que le vent marin vient fouetter les visages. Au fil de la traversée, les rives semblent se rapprocher, puis disparaître derrière nous. Ici, le temps paraît prendre un autre rythme en ce début d’après-midi. À mesure que l’on avance, Félir se dessine. D’abord une silhouette posée sur l’eau, puis une terre qui gagne en relief. Après 15 minutes en pirogue, le débarquement nous ramène rapidement à la réalité. La pirogue ralentit avant de venir se poser contre la berge. Mais ce qui frappe le visiteur au premier abord, c’est cette crue omniprésente. L’agitation de la ville semble loin. Sur cette île située au nord-ouest de Foundiougne, le temps semble suspendu aux caprices de Dame Nature. Ici, la crue dicte sa loi en cette période hivernale. Il faut faire des pirouettes pour pouvoir accéder au village. « Vous êtes venus au bon moment, comme cela, vous pourrez constater de visu ce que nous vivons au quotidien », nous souffle Babacar, notre guide. Pour cet insulaire, le verbe « patauger » est le plus conjugué sur cette île. « Aujourd’hui, ça va un peu mieux. Il y a des jours où l’eau arrive jusque dans nos salons », confie-t-il, tout en continuant à se frayer un chemin dans cette étendue d’eau. Une fois arrivés à destination, il nous conduit directement chez le premier citoyen de l’île : le chef de village. Des difficultés à la pelle « Soyez les bienvenus à Félir. Cela signifie en sérère “là où il fait bon vivre”, mais vous pouvez constater nos difficultés par vous-mêmes », dit El Hadji Bop, avec un sourire mi-figue mi-raisin. Après les salamalecs d’usage, le chef de village nous peint le tableau d’une île laissée en rade. « Nous avons tout pour vivre une belle vie. Mais les difficultés plombent l’ambiance », renchérit-il. Ce dernier n’hésite pas à nous faire le tour de l’île. Il nous amène chez l’imam. Ici, les difficultés sautent aux yeux. La crue a inondé une bonne partie de sa maison. « Nous avions une digue. Mais elle a cédé et, depuis, on vit la même situation chaque année », dit-il avec amertume. En sus de cela, il pointe du doigt des problèmes liés à l’enclavement, à l’accès à l’eau et à l’électricité. Les activités économiques sont aussi peu nombreuses. À Félir, les femmes n’ont qu’une seule source de revenus : la vente de crevettes. « C’est notre seule occupation, à défaut d’avoir du matériel pour la transformation », explique Ndeye Bop. Cette dernière souligne également les difficultés rencontrées par les femmes pour se soigner. « Nous n’avons qu’une case de santé. Mais elle ne nous est pas d’une grande utilité, faute de matériel et de personnel », fustige-t-elle. Santé, scolarité : des maux persistants Sur l’île, se soigner relève du véritable parcours du combattant. Ici, la seule structure de santé pour ces 896 habitants est plus mal en point que les insulaires qu’elle est censée accueillir. La vétusté du lieu frappe le visiteur dès les premiers abords. Une toiture en zinc ainsi que des chaises rouillées nous accueillent. Des lits rongés par la poussière, ainsi que l’absence de matériel sanitaire, font office de décor. Un état de fait que confirme Marie Ndong, relais communautaire. À l’en croire, la case de santé manque de tout. « Nous n’avons pas de matériel pour les accouchements. Les femmes sont obligées d’aller à Foundiougne pour bénéficier d’une prise en charge de qualité », explique Marie Ndong. Les femmes enceintes ne sont pas les seules à devoir prendre la pirogue pour rallier Foundiougne. Les jeunes apprenants sont aussi dans le désarroi. Gnima Bop, bachelière, se souvient encore des défis liés au trajet entre Félir et le lycée El Hadji Mamadou Diouf de Foundiougne. Lamine Diame embouche la même trompette. L’apprenant appelle les autorités à aider cette île où il est censé faire bon vivre. À Félir, l’eau finit toujours par se retirer, mais les difficultés, elles, restent. Chaque hivernage ramène son lot d’inquiétudes, de maisons inondées et de déplacements périlleux. Sur cette île où la nature impose sa loi, les habitants n’attendent pas que les eaux leur fassent une faveur. Ils attendent que les autorités leur tendent enfin la main. Car à force de patauger dans les eaux, Félir risque bien de continuer à se noyer dans l’indifférence. Arame NDIAYE (texte) – Mamoune DIOP (images et montages)

items.title: 246 tablettes Braille d’un coût de 12,5 millions de FCfa à des élèves malvoyants
items.description: La Journée internationale de la canne blanche a été célébrée ce 15 octobre à l’Arène nationale sur le thème : « Canne blanche, stop ». À l’occasion, l’État a annoncé la dotation de 246 nouvelles tablettes braille à des élèves aveugles et malvoyants. L’État a beaucoup fait et va apporter une meilleure assistance aux personnes atteintes de déficiences et pathologies visuelles. L’affirmation a été faite, hier, lors de la cérémonie officielle de la célébration de la Journée internationale de la canne blanche. Conseiller technique du ministre de la Famille, de l’Action sociale et des Solidarités, Adama Diouf a annoncé une bonne nouvelle aux personnes souffrant de difficultés visuelles : 246 tablettes Braille pour un coût de 12,5 millions de FCfa seront bientôt distribuées aux élèves aveugles et malvoyants. Il a ensuite fait la situation de la prévalence des déficiences et pathologies visuelles, notamment en convoquant les données du Recensement général de la population et de l’habitat (Rgph-5) de 2023, de l’Agence nationale de la statistique et de la démographie (Ansd). « La prévalence nationale du handicap est estimée à 7,3% chez les personnes d'un an et plus. Les difficultés “à voir” sont les plus fréquentes (3,9%), devant les difficultés à marcher (3,7%). Chez les personnes âgées de 65 ans et plus, les difficultés “à voir” atteignent 24,3% », a-t-il rappelé. Il a précisé que le handicap touche davantage les femmes (7,8%) que les hommes (6,8%), avec une prévalence quasi identique en milieu urbain et rural. À son avis, ces données illustrent l’ampleur du phénomène et fondent la nécessité de développer des stratégies préventives et curatives, et de promouvoir les droits humains des aveugles et malvoyants. « L’ex-coordonnateur du Programme national de lutte contre la cécité estimait la prévalence de la cécité entre 1 et 1,7%, voire 2%, au Sénégal. Ces données placent le handicap visuel au premier rang des handicaps au Sénégal », a-t-il indiqué. Cependant, Adama Diouf se réjouit du fait qu’au Sénégal, l’inclusion des personnes handicapées et la promotion de leurs droits fondamentaux trouvent un écho favorable dans l’agenda national de transformation, notamment dans l’Axe 2 de la Stratégie nationale de développement relatif au « Capital humain de qualité et l’équité sociale ». « Aujourd’hui, les résultats de certaines directives données par le chef de l’État portent sur la finalisation de l’intégralité des textes d’application de la loi d’orientation sociale relative au handicap, l’organisation des concertations nationales sur le handicap, l’élaboration de la stratégie nationale de promotion et de protection des personnes handicapées dont la validation institutionnelle sera bientôt effective, etc. » a affirmé le Conseiller technique du ministre de la Famille, de l’Action sociale et des Solidarités. Président de la Convergence des aveugles pour l’unité, la solidarité et l’entraide, Abdou Kogna Diop a salué les efforts que l’État déploie pour les personnes handicapées. Il a toutefois invité le pouvoir à faire davantage. Abdou DIOP

items.title: University of Ghana to reopen October 19 after GAUA suspends strike
items.description: The University of Ghana will reopen for the 2026/2027 academic year on October 19, following the suspension of the strike by the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA). In a notice dated October 16, 2026, the University said students would begin reporting to their halls of residence from October 19, while lectures are scheduled to commence on October 26. The notice, signed by the Pro Vice-Chancellor for Academic and Student Affairs, Professor Gordon A. Awandare, said the Business and Executive Committee took the decision at a meeting on October 16. According to the reopening schedule, the random allocation of beds is scheduled for October 16, while orientation for fresh students will take place from October 21 to 23. The University has urged students to pay the required fees and complete their academic registration online through the Students’ STS portal or the DiGradsys portal, in accordance with the prescribed procedures. Management has also asked students to comply with the registration requirements to ensure a smooth reopening and the commencement of lectures. The reopening follows the suspension of GAUA’s strike, which had disrupted academic activities at the University.

items.title: Rising mental health cases sign of improved help-seeking, not a new epidemic – Willingway CEO
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of The Willingway Recovery and Rehabilitation Centre (WRRC) at Ejisu-Asawase in the Ashanti region, Lydia Abena Manu Adofo, has observed that the rising mental health statistics in Ghana should not be misconstrued as a sudden epidemic of mental illness, but rather as a positive outcome of sustained education and sensitization efforts that are encouraging more people to seek professional help. For decades, she explained, stigma, misconceptions that mental illness was spiritual, and lack of information kept thousands of patients at home, in prayer camps, or on the streets, leaving health facilities with artificially low numbers. However, recent intensive public education has changed the narrative. Mrs. Lydia Abena Manu Adofo made the remarks when the facility’s executive management hosted retired US-based Ghanaian land-use planner and worldbeat music producer Dr. Kofi Newman, popularly known by his pen name Prof. Lungu, a long-time supporter of the centre. Mrs. Lydia Abena noted the country is reaping the benefits of years of advocacy by mental health professionals, NGOs and the media. “Looking at statistics from 2018, cases are rising over the years. People were not coming out for treatment, but through education and sensitization programmes that we were doing, they started going for treatment. Even though the cases are rising, we are happy because in previous years they were not coming out for treatment, so we didn’t have much data, but now they are coming,” she said. She noted that the development allows for better planning and resource allocation, as the true burden of mental illness is now becoming visible. Despite the positive trend in health-seeking behaviour, Mrs. Adofo expressed deep concern about the profile of cases her centre receives. She revealed that substance abuse remains one of the major causes of mental health cases recorded at his facility, with most cases diagnosed as drug-related psychosis. The victims, she said, are predominantly young men who have abused tramadol, cannabis (wee), cocaine, and other synthetic drugs. She warned that the trend is a ticking time bomb for national development, as it is stripping the country of its productive youth. “My advice to the youth is that they should completely stay away from drugs because it will end their careers and it will end their dreams. If they don’t stay away from drugs, the drugs will end their careers, end their dreams, and they will end up in the streets,” she cautioned. She called on parents, schools, religious bodies and community leaders to intensify drug prevention education and to create safe spaces for young people to discuss their challenges. She stressed that mental health conditions are treatable and that seeking early professional intervention remains the critical first step to recovery. The Willingway’s CEO used the occasion to make a passionate appeal to government to make rehabilitation services accessible to all Ghanaians by establishing at least one public rehabilitation centre and psychiatric hospital in each of the 16 regions. She lamented that patients in the Ashanti Region and the entire northern sector currently have to travel long distances to Pantang Hospital, Ankaful Psychiatric Hospital or Accra Psychiatric Hospital to access rehabilitation services after initial treatment. The cost of transportation, feeding, and accommodation for caregivers, she noted, discourages many families from completing the treatment process, leading to relapse. “The rehab should be so accessible. We should have some in all the regions. At least one in a region will help the people who are using drugs. If you have it here in Kumasi, you have to go to Pantang, Ankaful or Accra Psychiatric, but if we have a government rehab in the Ashanti Region, it will be so easy for the boys to get treatment,” she said. Mrs. Adofo argued that regional rehabilitation centres would not only reduce the financial burden on families but also ensure continuity of care, community reintegration and strong family support systems, which are critical to full recovery. Speaking during the visit, Dr. Kofi Newman (Prof. Lungu) commended Willingway for its contribution to mental health care in the Ashanti Region, but highlighted the wide gap between mental health treatment systems in developed countries, especially the United States, and that of Ghana. He noted that while the US has a more decentralized, well-funded system with community-based rehab centres, insurance coverage for mental health, and strong aftercare structures, Ghana still struggles with limited facilities, inadequate staffing, and low investment. He observed that in Ghana, most patients are forced to travel long distances for care, families bear the full cost of treatment, and aftercare is almost non-existent, increasing the rate of relapse. Dr. Newman called for increased government investment in mental health infrastructure, staffing and logistics, as well as strategic partnerships with private rehabilitation centres like Willingway to bridge the gap in service delivery. “Willingway is doing its part, but it cannot do it alone. Mental health is health, and it deserves the same attention we give to physical health,” he stressed. He called for stronger public-private partnerships and diaspora involvement in bridging the mental health care gap. The visit culminated in an awards presentation in recognition of commitment to mental health advocacy. The Executive Management of Willingway Recovery Center presented a citation of honour to Dr. Kofi Newman for his continuous dedication and contributions to the facility and his advocacy for improved mental health care in Ghana over the past decade. In return, Dr. Newman also presented a special award to the CEO of Willingway, Mrs. Lydia Abena Manu Adofo, in recognition of her dedication, sacrifice, and leadership in providing rehabilitation services and hope to persons living with mental health conditions and substance use disorders. Both parties pledged to deepen collaboration to promote mental health awareness and expand access to rehabilitation services in the country.

items.title: ECOWAS $250,000 donation for Ghana’s June flood victims arrives – Ablakwa
items.description: The Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, says the US$250,000 donation from the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) to support victims of Ghana’s June floods has arrived and been transferred to the Adventist Development and Relief Agency (ADRA) for distribution. In a post on Friday, October 16, Mr Ablakwa said the full donation, equivalent to about GH¢3 million, had been paid directly into the accounts of ADRA, which will administer the relief package. He said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) agreed to select ADRA as an independent implementing partner. According to the Minister, the arrangement is intended to ensure that the assistance reaches flood victims without government involvement in deciding who benefits. “Government will not be involved in the selection of who benefits from the relief package,” he stated. Mr Ablakwa made the announcement after inaugurating Ghana’s National Consultative Committee on Regional Integration (NCCRI) of ECOWAS. The committee is mandated to oversee ECOWAS’s regional integration activities and social interventions in Ghana. The Minister reaffirmed the government’s commitment to serving Ghanaians with integrity and transparency.

items.title: The Real Selling Point of Romantasy
items.description: This is an edition of the Books Briefing, our editors’ weekly guide to the best in books. Sign up for it here. Romantasy—the category of fiction in which the supernaturally gifted soar on the wings of love, and also sometimes of dragons—is incredibly successful. Its reigning queen, Sarah J. Maas, has sold about 75 million copies of her novels, my colleague Honor Jones reported in a recent Atlantic essay . The appeal of the genre, Jones found, isn’t just chiseled abs, smoldering gazes, and faerie frippery. Yes, there are hyper-athletic magical trysts, but “far more significant are feelings and friendships between the heroes: enchanted beings with relatable self-esteem issues who don’t just seek and fight but also yearn and banter as they face down enemies,” Jones writes. Readers stay for engaging and emotionally effective stories featuring characters they love. First, here are four new stories from The Atlantic ’s Books section: Good villains are hard to come by. This one’s great. The journalist and the manipulator Immigration is a poorly oiled machine. The man who wanted to understand every aspect of Jewish life Romantasy fans generally know that books like those in Maas’s mega-best-selling A Court of Thorns and Roses series—popularly known by the acronym ACOTAR —aren’t going to win the Pulitzer Prize. And they know that fantasy isn’t real life. “But if they’re snowed in—­or trapped by a pandemic, or up with a nursing newborn, or stuck in any of the ways humans tend to get stuck—­it can help to imagine” the possibility of magic, Jones writes. This reading experience doesn’t require the emotional tumult of picturing oneself in, say, Oliver Twist’s tiny 19th-century orphan shoes—or, more challenging, Fagin’s villainous boots. Instead, ACOTAR and its ilk make imagining easy: You may not know what it’s like to kiss a shape-shifter, but it’s exciting—seductive, even—to picture giving in to an attraction tinged with intrigue and mystery. And doing so is not necessarily less fulfilling than reading literary fare, because practicing this kind of creativity is good for us. It makes life’s hardships more bearable, as Jones indicates, and it also makes reality more interesting. If all we did was describe the mundane to one another, it would be difficult for any of us to have the kind of life worth writing stories about. Every queen-bee genre has its haters. Jones notes that plenty of people in the literary world “lament that the only books that sell now are faerie or dragon or elfpunk porn.” But a better approach would be to learn from romantasy’s success: We sometimes need a reminder that reading can simply be entertaining. And if entertainment comes from imagining what it might be like to have a hunky elf-king hanging around, well, where’s the harm in that? Illustration by Natalie Shields Those Books of Smut and Wonder By Honor Jones How Sarah J. Maas became the queen of romantasy Read the full article. What to Read The Fox Wife , by Yangsze Choo Choo’s novel, set in Manchuria in 1908, blends folklore and classic detective fiction, and adds a dash of fantasy—half of its characters are shape-shifting spirits who transform from foxes to humans and back again. These creatures are as clever and crafty as you might expect, and the narrative twists keep the reader in a state of high alert. What starts as a police procedural about the death of a high-class courtesan soon blossoms into a fantastical quest to break curses, rekindle lost love, and catch a murderer. Although it’s not overly long, the book has a mythic feeling, moving through time and space like an epic poem. Choo seamlessly combines narrative momentum and lush world-building, so the reader discovers the setting and uncovers the mystery alongside the novel’s endearing detective. — M. L. Rio From our list: Eight plot-heavy books that will keep you turning pages Out Next Week 📚 Redemption: Faith, Justice, and Sisterhood on Death Row , by Lawrence Wright 📚 Crooked Cross , by Sally Carson 📚 I Only Shout So You Can Hear Me , by Lil Jon with Paul Cantor Your Weekend Read Illustration by The Atlantic . Source: Gary Gershoff / Getty. Megyn Kelly’s Extreme Makeover By Sophie Gilbert Do you remember Megyn Kelly? I once walked past her in a Chicago O’Hare bathroom in 2016, shortly after Donald Trump had won his first presidential election, and was momentarily stopped in my tracks by both her nuclear-grade charisma and her pixie cut. For a woman to have short hair on Fox News, where Kelly was a star anchor at the time, seemed as seditious to the network’s established order as reading Judith Butler or Karl Marx live on air. But this was a moment during which Kelly seemed to be leaning into the role of crusader for women—speaking out about being sexually harassed by the former Fox News CEO Roger Ailes and so inflaming Trump with her rigorous questioning during one debate that he later insinuated on CNN that she must have had her period. Read the full article. When you buy a book using a link in this newsletter, we receive a commission. Thank you for supporting The Atlantic . items.title: Dr Mohamed Lamine Minka Kourouma : « La Guinée peut devenir le véritable poumon énergétique de l’Afrique de l’Ouest »
items.description: Enseignant-chercheur à l’Université Gamal Abdel Nasser de Conakry, ingénieur en génie électrique, écrivain et fondateur du cabinet Minkan Consulting, Dr Mohamed Lamine Minka Kourouma défend une approche du développement fondée sur la recherche scientifique, l’innovation et la valorisation des ressources locales. De la prévention des incendies d’origine électrique à Conakry à la transition énergétique à l’horizon 2040, en passant par le conseil stratégique et la littérature, il revient sur les grandes lignes de son parcours, ses engagements et sa vision pour la Guinée. Dans cet entretien qu'il a bien voulu nous accorder, il explique les motivations qui guident ses travaux de recherche, son ambition de contribuer à l’industrialisation du pays grâce à une énergie fiable et accessible, ainsi que le rôle de Minkan Consulting dans l’accompagnement des projets de développement. Il évoque également sa passion pour l’écriture et adresse un message aux jeunes étudiants et futurs ingénieurs guinéens. Lisez ! Mediaguinee : Vous êtes enseignant-chercheur, ingénieur en génie électrique, auteur et fondateur d'un cabinet d'études. Comment résumeriez-vous le fil conducteur de votre parcours ? Dr Mohamed Lamine Minka Kourouma : Mon fil conducteur est très simple : c'est la volonté d'apporter des réponses concrètes et scientifiques aux défis réels de la Guinée et de l'Afrique. Que ce soit dans un amphi à l'Université Gamal Abdel Nasser de Conakry, sur le terrain avec Minkan Consulting, ou à travers mes écrits, la finalité reste la même : mettre le savoir, l'innovation et la mémoire au service du développement socio-économique de notre pays. Mediaguinee : Vos travaux de recherche ne restent pas enfermés dans la théorie. Vous avez notamment travaillé sur les incendies d'origine électrique à Conakry. Pourquoi ce sujet précis ? Dr MohamedLamine Minka Kourouma : Parce que la science doit répondre aux souffrances quotidiennes de nos populations. Les incendies d'origine électrique causent chaque année des pertes humaines et matérielles considérables à Conakry. Mes recherches ont porté sur l'analyse des risques, la conformité des installations et la qualité des matériels électriques importés. Il était essentiel d'apporter un diagnostic scientifique rigoureux pour aider les décideurs et la population à adopter des normes de sécurité adaptées. Mediaguinée : Vous êtes très engagé sur la question de la transition énergétique et des ressources renouvelables. Quelle est votre vision pour la Guinée à l'horizon 2040 ? Dr Mohamed Lamine Minka Kourouma : La Guinée dispose d'un potentiel exceptionnel : hydroélectricité, énergie solaire, biomasse. Dans mon ouvrage Cap 2040 : Vision énergétique pour la Guinée, je défends l'idée que l'énergie est le socle de toute industrialisation. Pour transformer nos minerais sur place et créer des emplois pour notre jeunesse, il nous faut une puissance installée forte et stable. Mon combat est aussi d'intégrer pleinement la Guinée dans les réseaux d'interconnexion sous-régionaux comme le WAPP, le CLSG et l'OMVG. Notre pays a la capacité de devenir le véritable poumon énergétique de l'Afrique de l'Ouest. Mediaguinee : Qu'est-ce qui vous a poussé à créer le cabinet Minkan Consulting ? Dr MohamedLamine Minka Kourouma : La volonté de faire la liaison entre l'univers académique et les réalités du terrain. Les décideurs publics, les bailleurs et les investisseurs ont besoin d'études d'impact, de faisabilité et d'expertises ancrées dans la réalité locale. Avec Minkan Consulting, nous réalisons des diagnostics technico-économiques, nous accompagnons les projets de mini-réseaux solaires pour l'électrification rurale et nous apportons des conseils stratégiques pour la modernisation des infrastructures. Mediaguinee : Malgré un agenda scientifique et technique très chargé, vous trouvez le temps d'écrire des livres comme « Première classe Facely Koroma » ou « Au petit matin à Guéckédou ». D'où vient cette passion pour la plume ? Dr Mohamed Lamine Minka Kourouma : L'ingénieur construit les ponts et les réseaux, mais l'écrivain préserve l'âme et la mémoire d'un peuple. Pour moi, la technique et la culture sont indissociables. Première classe Facely Koroma est un hommage à l'éducation, au travail et à la résilience. Au petit matin à Guéckédou est un ancrage dans nos réalités sociales et régionales. Écrire me permet de transmettre des valeurs morales et civiques à la jeune génération. Mediaguinee : Quel message souhaitez-vous adresser aux jeunes étudiants et futurs ingénieurs que vous formez chaque jour ? Dr Mohamed Lamine Minka Kourouma : Je leur dis souvent que la Guinée de demain se construira par l'excellence, la rigueur et l'audace. Il ne faut pas attendre que les solutions viennent d'ailleurs. Nous devons nous former au plus haut niveau, maîtriser les technologies de pointe tout en valorisant nos ressources locales. La jeunesse guinéenne a un potentiel immense : il suffit de lui donner les outils, la confiance et le goût de l'effort. Propos recueillis par Youssouf Keita L’article Dr Mohamed Lamine Minka Kourouma : « La Guinée peut devenir le véritable poumon énergétique de l’Afrique de l’Ouest » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Pression fiscale en France : la taxe foncière a presque doublé en vingt ans
items.description: « Il faut arreter d'urgence de surtaxer les Francais et leurs entreprises », a enjoint la directrice de la Fondation pour la recherche sur les administrations et les politiques publiques (Ifrap), Agnes Verdier-Molinie, dans une interview parue ce 16 octobre dans les colonnes du Figaro , alors que le gouvernement Lecornu est en quete de 54 milliards d'euros supplementaires pour boucler le dernier budget de ce quinquennat Macron. La veille de cette publication, l'Union nationale des proprietaires immobiliers (UNPI) a rendu publique la vingtieme edition de son Observatoire national des taxes foncieres. On y apprend qu'en l'espace d'une generation — comme l'ont image certains medias francais —, cet impot a presque double, avec une hausse moyenne de 93,4 % entre 2005 et 2025. « Son montant a ainsi quasiment double en vingt ans alors que l'inflation, dont on parle tous les jours, n'a crû sur vingt ans que de 36,8 %, tandis que les loyers n'ont augmente que de 27 % », a souligne le president de l'UNPI, Sylvain Grataloup, cite par Le Parisien . Vers une pression fiscale record en 2027 Les proprietaires subissent a la fois les taux appliques aux biens immobiliers, votes par les collectivites, et les valeurs locatives cadastrales estimees par l'administration fiscale. Selon Le Figaro , les premiers ont augmente de 32,2 % en vingt ans, tandis que les valeurs locatives cadastrales ont progresse de 46,3 % sur la meme periode. Face a cet impot, tous les proprietaires ne sont pas loges a la meme enseigne. a Paris, dirige par le Parti socialiste depuis le debut des annees 2000, la taxe fonciere a explose de 261,2 % — parallelement a la hausse de la dette de la ville —, un taux qui ne prend pas en compte la taxe d'enlevement des ordures menageres. a l'oppose, on retrouve Colombes, dans les Hauts-de-Seine, ou cet impot a progresse de 36 %. Presentant cet impot comme « extremement injuste », l'economiste Thomas Piketty a appele, le 15 octobre sur BFMTV, a « passer a un impot progressif sur le patrimoine net d'emprunt », en somme a faire payer davantage ceux qui sont pleinement proprietaires de leur logement. Selon lui, cela reviendrait a « une baisse de la taxe fonciere pour 90 % des Francais ». Pour rappel, la France dispute au Danemark le titre de pays de l'OCDE qui taxe le plus. Apres une pression fiscale atteignant 43,9 % du PIB en 2026, Bercy se pencherait sur une hausse de ce taux a 44,2 % l'annee prochaine.

items.title: FRC operated without board for over 13 years, nominee tells senate
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu’s nominee for chairman of the board of the Fiscal Responsibility Commission (FRC), Abdullahi Saidu, has told the Senate that the commission has operated without a board for more than 13 years, a situation he said has hindered its operations. Saidu spoke on Wednesday when he appeared before the Senate Committee on Finance for screening alongside six other nominees. He said the absence of a board had left the commission with significant institutional challenges, adding that the incoming board would have to rebuild its operations if confirmed. Saidu said the commission was expected to establish offices in at least one location in each of the six geopolitical zones but currently operated only from Abuja. He pledged to work with the National Assembly and other stakeholders to strengthen the commission and improve its capacity to discharge its mandate. The nominee also disclosed that the commission lacked prosecutorial powers, explaining that it could investigate cases and forward its findings to the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice for prosecution. He said the proposed board would seek a review of the law establishing the commission to strengthen its independence and operational capacity. Saidu further pledged to improve government revenue by strengthening the monitoring of operating surpluses generated by government-owned and other organisations covered by the commission’s mandate. According to him, some revenue-generating organisations fail to remit the appropriate share of their operating surpluses to the Federal Government. He said such organisations were expected to remit 80 per cent of their operating surpluses to the Consolidated Revenue Fund while retaining 20 per cent for their operations. “Because the commission is not informed, so they just declare whatever they feel they want to declare,” he said. Saidu assured the committee that, if confirmed, the board would strengthen monitoring to ensure that the appropriate revenues were declared and remitted. He expressed confidence that the commission’s performance could improve within a year, provided it received the necessary support from the National Assembly and other stakeholders. The screening was presided over by Senator Lere Oyewumi, vice-chairman of the committee, who represented its chairman, Senator Sani Musa. Addressing the nominees, Oyewumi said managing the commission required specialised knowledge and preparation, noting that the assignment differed from other public service roles. He urged them to participate in retreats with experts and undertake extensive reading to prepare for the responsibilities ahead. Senator Osita Ngwu, representing Enugu West, moved a motion for Saidu and the other nominees to take a bow and leave, while Senator Sadiq Suleiman Umar, representing Kwara North, seconded the motion. The other nominees screened alongside Saidu were Muhammad Asma’u, Muhammad Makama, Suleiman Gidado, Louis Ndukwe, Amechi Ugwele and Olaniyi Onikola. The committee is expected to submit its report to the Senate for further legislative action. items.title: 10 phones with 10,000mAh batteries or more

Unlike conventional smartphones, which often have batteries ranging from 4,000mAh to 6,000mAh, these devices offer substantially larger capacities that can reduce the need for frequent charging. While most phones in this category are rugged devices designed for demanding environments, newer models are increasingly combining large batteries with features such as AMOLED displays, fast charging and 5G connectivity. However, a larger battery often means a heavier and thicker phone. Buyers should also distinguish between models with exactly 10,000mAh batteries and those offering higher capacities. Here are 10 smartphones with batteries rated at 10,000mAh or more. 1. Its advertised specifications include a 10,000mAh battery, 100W fast charging, a 6.83-inch AMOLED display and 5G connectivity. These features position it as an option for users who want a large battery alongside the everyday functions of a mainstream smartphone. Buyers should verify the model name and specifications with the manufacturer or retailer before purchasing. 2. realme P4 Power — 10,001mAh The realme P4 Power is designed for users who prioritise battery endurance without giving up modern smartphone features. It features a 10,001mAh silicon-carbon battery, an AMOLED display with a 144Hz refresh rate, a MediaTek Dimensity 7400 Ultra processor and 80W fast charging. The high-refresh-rate screen is suited to smooth scrolling and gaming, while the large battery provides substantial capacity for extended daily use. 3. realme Narzo Power — 10,001mAh The realme Narzo Power is another smartphone in the large-battery category, combining a 10,001mAh battery with modern display and charging technology. Its specifications include an AMOLED display, a high refresh rate and fast charging, making it an option for people who spend considerable time gaming, watching videos or using mobile applications. As with other recently introduced models, availability and specifications should be confirmed for the buyer’s market. 4. The model is presented as an option for users seeking extended battery life alongside everyday smartphone performance. However, its official model identity, specifications and market availability should be independently verified before it is included in a purchasing shortlist. 5. Oukitel WP100 Titan — 33,000mAh The Oukitel WP100 Titan stands out for its 33,000mAh battery, which is more than three times the capacity of a typical 10,000mAh phone. Designed for demanding outdoor use, the rugged smartphone targets people who work in remote locations, travel extensively or spend long periods away from electrical outlets. Its enormous battery makes it suitable for users who value endurance over a compact design. However, its size and weight make it less convenient for people who prefer lightweight everyday smartphones. 6. Ulefone Armor 29 Pro — 21,200mAh The Ulefone Armor 29 Pro is a rugged smartphone designed for demanding environments, including outdoor activities and industrial work. Its 21,200mAh battery provides considerably more capacity than conventional smartphones, making it attractive to users who need a device that can remain operational for extended periods. Oukitel WP300 — 16,000mAh The Oukitel WP300 combines a 16,000mAh battery with a rugged design intended for outdoor use. Blackview BV9300 Pro — 15,080mAh The Blackview BV9300 Pro is a rugged Android smartphone with a 15,080mAh battery. The model may appeal to buyers who want a substantial battery without moving to the exceptionally large capacities offered by devices such as the Oukitel WP100 Titan. 9. items.title: 2027: Ndigbo with PVCs back Tinubu — Obidike
items.description: A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Chief Obidike Chukwuebuka, has expressed confidence that Ndigbo will rally behind President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, urging eligible voters in the South-East to make their votes count. Obidike, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Clarivo Oil and Gas, said the South-East could no longer afford to approach national politics solely from the standpoint of opposition, urging voters to assess the Tinubu administration based on infrastructure, representation, economic opportunities and federal presence in the region. Speaking in an interview, he identified the establishment of the South-East Development Commission (SEDC) as a significant institutional response to the region’s longstanding demand for coordinated federal intervention and development. He also cited the approval of the South-East Investment Company, an investment vehicle designed to mobilise capital and accelerate industrial and infrastructure development across the five South-East states, with initial funding of N150 billion. According to him, the investment framework, alongside the SEDC, provides a platform for the region to pursue large-scale development beyond the limitations of individual political administrations. Obidike further pointed to the Federal Government’s support for the South-East Vision 2050 development blueprint, a long-term regional framework intended to promote coordinated economic planning, industrialisation, infrastructure development and regional integration. On road infrastructure, the APC chieftain cited the reconstruction and rehabilitation of the Enugu-Onitsha Expressway, describing it as one of the region’s most important economic corridors. He also referenced the 107-kilometre Enugu-Onitsha Expressway project, being reconstructed under the Infrastructure Development and Refurbishment Investment Tax Credit Scheme, with MTN Nigeria involved in the project. Other projects he highlighted included the Enugu-Port Harcourt Expressway, particularly the Umuahia-Aba section; the Enugu-Ninth Mile-Makurdi Expressway; the Enugu-Abakaliki Highway; the Okigwe-Owerri Road; the Onitsha-Owerri Road; the Aba-Ikot Ekpene Road; and the Owerri-Aba Road. Obidike also highlighted what he described as increased federal attention to education and healthcare infrastructure in the South-East. Among the projects he cited were the Federal College of Education, Bende, Abia State; the Federal University of Medical and Health Sciences, Item, Bende, Abia State; and the Federal University, Okigwe, Imo State. He also pointed to the Federal Government’s approval for the upgrade of the University of Nigeria Teaching Hospital (UNTH), Enugu, as well as investments in medical facilities at the institution. Obidike, who also chairs Clarivo Holdings Limited and Bidiks Nigeria Limited, said the central issue for voters in the South-East should be whether their political choices advance the interests of the people, rather than whether they support the party controlling the Federal Government. He argued that supporting an incumbent president did not amount to abandoning regional interests, adding that the 2027 presidential election would provide an opportunity for voters in the region to reassess their political choices. The APC chieftain expressed confidence that Ndigbo across the five South-East states, as well as those residing in other parts of the country, would rally behind Tinubu in the election. He urged eligible voters to participate in the electoral process, stressing that the region should not allow the opportunity to secure greater federal attention, investment and development to slip away. The post 2027: Ndigbo with PVCs back Tinubu — Obidike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Blue Nile initiative condemns arbitrary arrests targeting civilians over alleged family ties
items.description: The Civil Society Initiative in the Blue Nile region has condemned arbitrary arrests targeting civilians on suspicion of family or tribal links to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) or the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-North (SPLM-N) led by Abdelaziz El Hilu. Ali Hajo, the initiative’s secretary-general, told Radio Dabanga that security forces had arrested Elrih Younis Babiker, Elbagir Elamin Saad and Jabara Abdallah in El Roseires and taken them to an unknown location while blindfolded. He said there were reports that the detainees had been tortured. Hajo said arrests had affected civilians across Blue Nile, particularly in Ed Damazin, El Roseires locality , Wad El Mahi and Geisan locality, with families often unaware of their relatives’ whereabouts. He said some detainees had been held for one to two years without investigation or charge. The initiative warned that arbitrary arrests, alleged torture and enforced disappearances threaten peace, deepen grievances and undermine social cohesion. It called on the authorities to disclose the whereabouts of detainees, release those held without legal grounds or bring them before a court and allow families and lawyers access to them. It also urged human rights organisations, the United Nations and international bodies to investigate alleged violations and help protect civilians. Hajo warned that the security and humanitarian situation in Blue Nile was deteriorating, with displaced people facing dire conditions and drone attacks reportedly targeting civilian areas, including homes. The initiative called for an immediate end to arbitrary arrests and urged the authorities to uphold the rule of law and protect civilians regardless of their identity or family ties. Share article The post Blue Nile initiative condemns arbitrary arrests targeting civilians over alleged family ties appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

items.title: What Newsrooms Should Know Before They Take Money From OpenAI
items.description: As a newsroom executive, I have long tried to resist appeals to vet donors to nonprofit journalism for their politics or even the savoriness of their business practices. When you do that, you raise questions about whether you could fairly cover any potential donors on your banned list, and you also run the risk of offering some sort of implicit endorsement to the rest. Both of those perceptions are antithetical to the independent stance that good journalism requires. To take one notorious example, we never received a check from the Koch family’s interests when I was running the business side of ProPublica, but I would have been happy to take it if we had. Nor am I one of those people who think that it makes sense to refuse corporate contributions. Almost all major donors derive the money they are offering from a successful corporation. With that said, I want to offer some cautionary thoughts on the largesse from the company that has become the leading corporate supporter of American journalism, OpenAI. In gifts through its People-First AI Fund, and in large grants disbursed through the American Journalism Project and the Lenfest Institute for Journalism (both occasional consulting clients of mine), OpenAI has distributed $25 million in cash to U.S. newsrooms in the past few years, a large multiple of the journalism grants from Microsoft and Google. OpenAI has also made a number of significant one-off gifts, so its total is considerably larger. Anthropic has not yet joined this party. ( The Atlantic has a content-licensing agreement with OpenAI, although it does not receive grant funding from the company.) I know that the money is needed, and I am not questioning the uses to which it is currently being put. I think newsrooms need to be more creative in the use of AI, not less; more innovative; and less afraid of the implications for particular kinds of work that may become outmoded. Here’s what I think the recipients need to bear in mind. The company’s motivation here is not altruistic . OpenAI says that its intent is “to benefit all of humanity,” but we know that some people there and elsewhere worry that it is, in fact, going to end up snuffing out humanity. We also see that, in the face of such warnings, the company races along, its CEO announcing that “the world should accept some bad things happening.” More narrowly, the firm’s spending on supporting news is almost certainly seen internally as a form of marketing and public relations, helping to spur product adoption and perhaps blunt any impulses toward regulation or taxation, both of which seem to be crucially and urgently necessary. The money may be material to us, but it isn’t to them . It should be sobering, for instance, that OpenAI spent roughly the same amount of money trying to intervene in a single Manhattan congressional primary this past spring as it has in newsroom funding over the years through Lenfest. [ Matteo Wong: OpenAI has gone rogue ] Our worldviews are at fundamental variance . The core principles of journalism focus on the search for accuracy with fairness and the discovery of truth. The essence of the business of generative artificial intelligence seems to be the maximization of profit , whether or not other goals are achieved. The spigot could shut off at any time, and likely eventually will . We have been down this road before with tech firms, and need to assume that this funding won’t be sustained, and shouldn’t be part of any plan for sustainability. Facebook was a significant funder of news until it not only wasn’t, but then took steps to choke off the flow of news to its users. Google purported to be especially solicitous of news until, in my view , it detected insufficient gratitude and greater support for regulation (especially in Canada) and largely reversed course. ( The Atlantic has received grant funding in the past from Facebook and Google but no longer accepts such grants to fund its journalism.) Inside the velvet glove is a mailed fist . Journalists should never forget that there is significant evidence that OpenAI has built its enormous machine in small but significant (at least to us) part by appropriating our intellectual property without compensation. That’s a nice way of saying that the company is arguing in court that it has the right to take our lifeblood while laying waste to important parts of our business. This is ultimately a legal question, but one in which the company—and, to be sure, its competitors at Anthropic, Google, Meta, and Microsoft—is our adversary. The stakes in those fights may be existential for newsrooms; they will not be for the platforms. Transparency is always a good idea . When creating new AI tools or devising new methods or products using AI that are ultimately funded by an AI company, journalists owe it to their readers, listeners, and viewers to let them know about that funding. Don’t limit the disclosure to an intermediary source through which the money passed. Innovation needs to be coupled with accountability . Even as OpenAI and, to a lesser extent, some of its competitors are paying newsrooms for more rapid and clever adoption of their products and services, it’s very important that anyone taking this funding also invest commensurately in increased accountability for these behemoths and the havoc they are wreaking in some local communities, many funding streams, and, moving forward, job markets. I do have faith in the ability of editors and publishers to maintain editorial independence from funders; I have seen it in action many times. But the larger the portions of food on offer, the greater the temptation not to bite the hand offering it. We need to help one another to resist this, including by pointing out compromises among colleagues if and when we see them. [ Jessica Lessin: Media companies are making a huge mistake with AI ] One important caveat: I am far less concerned about the explosion almost certainly ahead in individual philanthropy derived from AI than I am about the direct provision of corporate funds. There may be issues with some individuals, of course. But the multiplicity of likely funders will help, as will their varying motivations. The truth is that corporate philanthropy has always been something of an oxymoron. The duty of corporations is to their shareholders, and specifically to the maximizing of shareholder value. Journalists can take some comfort that, in companies with more enlightened management, this objective is sought over the long run, which may more closely align with societal interests. Managers with more limited vision, as well as those so enamored of their own capabilities as to conflate society’s objectives with their own, present a less happy case. All of us in the news business would do well to look hard at which of these types we believe are leading the AI revolution today. This article was adapted from a post on Richard J. Tofel’s Substack, Second Rough Draft.
